content:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager alert triggered: service=redwood-model-serving-canary, alert=5xx-rate-spike, threshold=10%/2m. PagerDuty incident PD-8672 created. Affected route: /v1/generate (canary pool v2.14)

pagerduty-bot: PD-8672 — page fired (high) -> escalation policy: infra-oncall. Link: https://pd.example/incidents/PD-8672

alex (oncall): acked. I'll take. Oncall who? @maria can you pull up canary graphs?

maria (sre): looking. Grafana: https://grafana/redwood/d/serving/canary?from=-15m&to=now — seeing error% jump at 1841509800, 5xxs mostly 502/504. Latency also up from 200ms -> 3-8s for some requests. CPU/GPU usage normal, but connection timeouts spiked.

raj (eng): last deploy changed KV-cache eviction thresholds + a tiny change to upstream health checks in the canary config (v2.14). Could be failing fast on certain prefix cache hits.

lisa (support): support thread: 3 customers reported timeouts for embeddings generation in last 10m. No large-scale data loss, but UX timeouts. Ticket ids: SUP-912, SUP-913, SUP-914. They escalated to AE.

alex (oncall): quick triage plan: 1) try suppress noisy alerts to avoid paging every minute 2) if errors persist, rollback canary to v2.13 3) scale canary pool to absorb traffic while rollback completes. Agree? :+1:

maria (sre): suppressing alert temporarily for PD-8672 (15m) to avoid pages while we act. Adding annotation: "investigating - rollback candidate".

pagerduty-bot: PD-8672 status: acknowledged by alex (oncall). Notifications suppressed (15m) by maria.

raj (eng): I recommend immediate rollback. Change in health check aggressively marking backends unhealthy. If we keep routing to this canary, users will see transient failures.

alex (oncall): ok rolling back canary to v2.13. Performing controlled rollback on canary pool now. Will post command output.

alex (oncall): running:
```bash
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/canary-pool redwood-serving=redwood-inference:v2.13 --record\kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/canary-pool --timeout=5m
```

alex (oncall): rollout initiated. Current pods terminating, new pods starting.

maria (sre): while rollback runs, doing rate-limit routing pin: route 10% -> canary, 90% -> prod. Setting in routing service now.

tom (ops-lead): I'll scale the prod pool +2 replicas temporarily to keep latency down during change. Running: `kubectl scale deploy/prod-pool --replicas=12 -n inference`

alex (oncall): rollback completed. rollout status: success. Output:
```
deployment "canary-pool" rolled out successfully
status: 3 old replicas terminated, 3 new replicas available
```

maria (sre): monitoring graphs — error rate back to baseline within ~45s after traffic shift. Latency recovering to ~220ms.

lisa (support): notified customers: SUP-912/913/914 updated with incident note and ETA for full resolution. No billing adjustments yet, customers asked for RCA.

raj (eng): created PR to revert aggressive health-check behavior and add more conservative retry logic: https://git.internal/pr/5593. Will coordinate hotfix if tests pass.

alex (oncall): PD-8672 — marking resolved in PagerDuty; manual closure by oncall after rollback and monitoring window.

pagerduty-bot: PD-8672 status: resolved by alex (oncall).

tom (ops-lead): handing off postmortem to maria and raj. Maria, can you own service-level timeline and mitigation notes? Raj, please own root cause + fix PR. I'll coordinate customer comms with Lisa.

maria (sre): taking timeline + postmortem. I'll include alerts, suppression decision, rollback command, and monitoring screenshots. ETA for draft: 2 hours.

raj (eng): will prioritize hotfix and run canary again behind a stricter traffic ramp.

alex (oncall): thanks team. tagging incident done. If anything creeps back, re-open PD and re-page. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident PD-8672 closed. Summary: canary v2.14 caused health-check/kv-cache interaction -> high 5xx rate; suppressed alert, rolled back to v2.13, scaled prod pool temporarily; customers notified; owners assigned for postmortem.
